newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swaps - Jet/gas oil regrade at discount.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swaps - Jet/gas oil regrade at discount.

text.p: Singapore swaps jet/gasoil regrade slipped into discount at midday on Wednesday, succumbing to pressure from the physical market which has seen jet values trailing gas oil over the past two weeks, traders and brokers said.
April regrade was traded at a 10-cent-per-barrel discount late on Tuesday. Current April regrade was quoted at -0.25/+0.50 cents and May at -0.50/+0.15 cents.
Brokers said swaps jet/gas oil regrade have finally buckled under the pressure of negative spread in the physical market.
"Jet swaps have been firmer than gas oil despite the weaker jet prices in the cash (physical) market," a broker said.
In the physical market, jet fuel has fallen below gas oil quotes since two weeks ago with the current spread seen around a discount of $2.20-$2.30 per barrel.

The negative spread was due to poor regional demand for jet fuel, as Indonesia was not expected to buy very much for April, while gas oil remained supported by a local trader's buying spree and healthy purchases by India in its recent tender for May arrival cargoes.
April gas oil was last quoted at $26.55/$26.75 barely moved from Tuesday's $26.65/$26.75. May was quoted at $25.40/$25.50.
In the fuel oil market, the April/May spread has also eased back into backwardation.
Levels were quoted at par most of Tuesday but current April/May spreads were at a 25-cent backwardation. April swaps were at $97.50/$98.50 and May at $97.25/$98.25.
Brokers said buying support from a local trader who bought two cargoes on Tuesday helped to push the prompt April month higher.
The trader purchased two 20,000-tonne cargoes of 180-cst grade at $99.50 and $101 for April loading.
